text:
Olivia (support): heads up — getting a spike of customer tickets for 5xx / timeouts on hosted inference. They all look like cache-related failures. Early batch: 50+ errors in 25m.

Olivia (support): example ticket: customer 'AcmeMaps' saw repeated 502s from POST /v1/generate, request_id=req_20240315_9fb2, model=gpt-redwood-7b, latency before failure ~ 1200ms then timeout.

Olivia (support): logs attached by customer show: `GatewayError: upstream cache timeout` and `KVFetchError: redis timeout`. Also saw `ERR max number of clients reached` in our logs for the cache client.

Sophia (SRE): thanks. I'm looking at infra dashboards. Cache (redis-primary) error rate jumped at 1849000000. Lots of `READONLY` and `MISCONF` style errors on the pod logs. Could be RDB snapshot thrash or OOM eviction panic.

Ravi (Infra): adding more detail — memcached node in region-us-west also had connection resets around same window. So both KV layers show instability. Possible cascading failure: large request burst + long-running prefix retrievals filling up connections.

Marco (oncall): @Sophia can you paste the failing pod logs and `kubectl get pods -n infra-redis`?

Sophia (SRE): running quick checks now.

ops-bot: [monitoring] Alert: redis-primary (infra-redis/us-west) high latency and connection errors — firing at 1849000032.

Sophia (SRE): pod list snapshot:
```
NAME                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
redis-primary-0         1/1     Running   3          12d
redis-replica-0         1/1     Running   0          12d
memcached-usw-0         1/1     Running   2          30d
```

Sophia (SRE): tail of redis-primary logs:
```
[1849000029] "MISCONF Redis is configured to save RDB snapshots, but the current user has been blocked because the RDB file could not be created"
[1849000030] "-ERR max number of clients reached"
[1849000041] "OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'"
```

Olivia (support): any quick customer-facing mitigation we can suggest? Right now they're getting 502/504 when we try to fetch prefix KV during generation.

Sophia (SRE): short-term: disable prefix/KV caching for affected route(s) so requests hit cold model path (slower, but avoids cache dependency). I can push a traffic rule to bypass cache for the tenant(s) hitting errors.

Ravi (Infra): also going to increase redis `maxclients` and check disk space for RDB writes. If MISCONF is due to disk full on the node, restarting will not fix until free space available.

Marco (oncall): action plan:
- Sophia: push per-tenant bypass for prefix cache (10m) — owner
- Ravi: scale redis/adjust maxclients and free disk if needed — owner
- Olivia: update customers with interim workaround + ETA — owner

Sophia (SRE): doing bypass now. Patch payload I used in console:
```
PATCH /admin/route/acmemaps
{ "prefix_cache_enabled": false, "note": "temp bypass due to redis errors 18490000" }
```
Response: 200 OK — route updated.

Sophia (SRE): applying rate-limited rollout, target tenants: AcmeMaps + 3 others that reported identical trace signatures.

Olivia (support): sending quick message to customers:
"We're seeing degraded performance due to our cache tier. We've temporarily disabled prefix caching for your traffic to restore availability; you may see slightly increased latency while we remediate. We're on it and will update in 30 minutes."

Ravi (Infra): diagnostics I'm running:
```
kubectl exec -n infra-redis redis-primary-0 -- redis-cli INFO memory
kubectl exec -n infra-redis redis-primary-0 -- redis-cli CONFIG GET maxclients
kubectl exec -n infra-redis redis-primary-0 -- df -h /data
```
Findings:
- used_memory ~ 96% of maxmemory
- maxclients = 1000
- /data usage 99% -> RDB writes failing (MISCONF).

Ravi (Infra): root cause likely disk pressure on redis node; RDB snapshot attempted, couldn't write -> MISCONF -> write commands blocked -> clients starve -> `maxclients` hit -> connection resets -> downstream 5xx.

Sophia (SRE): immediate remediation: free space on disk (moving old snapshots), trigger manual BGSAVE disabled for now, restart redis-primary with smaller RDB frequency. I'll coordinate safe steps.

Marco (oncall): do it during low traffic window? We already disabled prefix cache; that should reduce pressure, but we still need to clear disk.

Ravi (Infra): performing quick cleanup: `rm /var/lib/redis/dump-old.rdb` and moved archives to NFS. Then bumping maxclients->2000 and restarting redis-primary gracefully.

ops-bot: [deploy] redis-primary pod restart scheduled at 1849000410 by Ravi.

Sophia (SRE): after restart logs:
```
[1849000502] "Background saving terminated with success"
[1849000510] "Ready to accept connections"
```
Error rate fell but some memcached resets still present.

Ravi (Infra): memcached had a restart loop due to old config: connection pooling too small for our increased concurrency. Patching memcached config `-c 10000` to allow more concurrent connections.

Sophia (SRE): monitoring shows 5xx count drop from 120/min -> 4/min over 10 minutes. Latency stabilized around normal for bypassed tenants.

Olivia (support): updating affected customers with root cause + remediation steps: disabled prefix cache, freed disk, restarted redis, scaled memcached. Promised a postmortem.

Olivia (support): sample message to customers:
"TL;DR: We caused service disruptions when our cache node ran out of disk space, which prevented writes and led to connection errors. We temporarily disabled prefix caching for your traffic to restore requests. We've cleaned disk space, restarted cache nodes, and increased connection limits; normal behavior resumed. We'll follow up with a detailed postmortem and permanent fixes. Apologies for the impact."

Marco (oncall): next steps (action items):
- Ravi: verify long-term disk retention policy and alert thresholds (disk >85% notify)
- Sophia: add graceful fallback on cache client: if redis returns MISCONF or OOM, auto-fallback to cold path rather than fail the request
- Olivia: consolidate ticket replies and schedule customer postmortem email
- Engineering: evaluate moving RDB snapshots to separate disk or S3 offload

Ravi (Infra): I've created infra ticket INF-482: "Redis disk pressure -> MISCONF -> API 5xx" with links to logs and commands. Assigning to infra-storage team.

Sophia (SRE): also creating runbook update: detect MISCONF and auto-disable prefix cache for impacted routes, with manual approval required to re-enable.

Olivia (support): will queue a postmortem draft once we have all timelines.

Marco (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread pinned for follow-ups. If any new customers pop up with same trace pattern, add them here and we'll apply bypass immediately. :thumbsup:

Sophia (SRE): marking incident status: mitigated — monitoring. Will update to resolved after 24h with no regression.

ops-bot: [monitoring] All clear: redis-primary healthy at 1849000750.

Olivia (support): closing loop with customers now. Will attach incident ref INF-482 in replies.
